blogs.title: Who Gets the Penalties? 8th Circuit Limits Private Enforcement of Minnesota Wage Laws
blogs.description: This post analyzes the Eighth Circuit's statutory interpretation of the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act (MPWA), specifically holding that private employees cannot recover 'average daily wage penalties' under Minn. Stat. § 181.101. We examine the court's reliance on legislative intent and the distinction between the Commissioner's enforcement powers and an employee's substantive right to wages, discussing the implications for class action leverage in Minnesota employment litigation.

blogs.title: Made Whole but Not Mooted? Standing for Civil Penalties After Back Pay
blogs.description: Focusing on the MFLSA claim, this post explores the jurisdictional tension when an employer pays all back wages and liquidated damages, but the employee seeks statutory penalties payable to the state. We discuss the application of Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw regarding mootness and voluntary cessation, and how the Eighth Circuit's remand highlights the continuing standing requirements for citizen plaintiffs seeking civil penalties in wage theft cases.

blogs.title: Don't Save It for the Brief: Waiver and Pleading Requirements in Employment Appeals
blogs.description: This post highlights the procedural pitfalls in Cohen, where the Eighth Circuit affirmed the dismissal of MWTA and injunctive relief claims due to waiver and improper pleading. We review the court's strict adherence to Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15 and the necessity of supporting appellate arguments with legal authority, offering practical lessons for employment practitioners on preserving claims throughout litigation.
